how_to_query:
DISCOVERY: https://www.morningstar.com/careers returns HTTP 202 with a 0-byte body (bot-shielded, useless). The Workday tenant is `morningstar` on the wd5 pod. I brute-forced the site name; `Morningstar` (and lowercase `morningstar`) return 200, everything else 404.

1) LIST ALL JOBS (218 total as of 24 Sep 2026), paginate with offset in steps of 20:
curl -s -X POST "https://morningstar.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/wday/cxs/morningstar/Morningstar/jobs" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"appliedFacets":{},"limit":20,"offset":0,"searchText":""}'

2) FILTER TO INDIA (fuzzy, returns 52):
curl -s -X POST "https://morningstar.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/wday/cxs/morningstar/Morningstar/jobs" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"appliedFacets":{},"limit":20,"offset":0,"searchText":"India"}'

3) FILTER TO INTERNSHIPS ONLY (workerSubType facet = Intern, returns 8 globally, ZERO in India):
curl -s -X POST "https://morningstar.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/wday/cxs/morningstar/Morningstar/jobs" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"appliedFacets":{"workerSubType":["61e5b2ad7cc44ec08ae855d7e0f4dd7a"]},"limit":20,"offset":0,"searchText":""}'

4) FULL JOB DETAIL INCLUDING VERBATIM QUALIFICATIONS (append the externalPath from the list response):
curl -s -H "Accept: application/json" \
  "https://morningstar.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/wday/cxs/morningstar/Morningstar/job/Mumbai/Quantitative-Analyst--New-Product-Development_REQ-058340"
The response has jobPostingInfo.jobDescription (HTML), .location, .additionalLocations, .startDate (real posting date), .jobReqId, .externalUrl (the human apply link), .timeType.

5) HUMAN APPLY URL PATTERN (verified HTTP 200):
https://morningstar.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/morningstar/job/<City>/<Slug>_<REQID>

TWO ADDITIONAL SITES ON THE SAME TENANT (both are strict subsets of the main feed, no unique India roles):
- .../wday/cxs/morningstar/MorningstarDBRS/jobs  -> 50 jobs, 3 in India (REQ-058189, REQ-058408, REQ-057834 - all already in the main feed)
- .../wday/cxs/morningstar/Sustainalytics/jobs   -> 200 OK but 0 jobs (empty/retired site)
No PitchBook-specific Workday site exists on this tenant; PitchBook reqs (REQ-058054, REQ-055994, REQ-058243) are posted inside the main Morningstar feed with legal entity "PitchBook Data, Inc".

No WebFetch or WebSearch was needed. Everything above was obtained with plain curl.

SHORT VERSION: Morningstar has a real, well-built campus machine - but as of today it is 100% CHICAGO-BASED and 100% US-WORK-AUTHORISATION-GATED. There is currently ZERO India internship, ZERO India graduate programme, and the one India entry-level pipeline that does exist (the Mumbai "Apprentice" req) explicitly bars B.Tech holders. This is the single most important finding for this candidate.

=== A) THE CHICAGO 2027 CAMPUS PROGRAMMES - ALL OPEN RIGHT NOW, ALL CLOSE 5 OCTOBER 2026 ===
Every one of these carries the verbatim line "This role will be posted until October 5, 2026." So applications are OPEN, with an 11-day window from today (24 Sep 2026).

1. Morningstar Development Program - Equity Research | REQ-058267 | Chicago | posted 8 Sep 2026
   https://morningstar.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/morningstar/job/Chicago/Morningstar-Development-Program---Equity-Research_REQ-058267
   Verbatim graduation window: "A bachelor's degree to be completed no later than May 2027"
   Verbatim: "We are accepting applicants with zero to two years of full-time work experience. While we look for individuals who have an interest in investing, we welcome all fields of study. All positions are based in our Chicago office."
   Base salary $83,000. THIS IS THE ONLY MORNINGSTAR PROGRAMME WHOSE GRADUATION WINDOW MATCHES OMKAR EXACTLY (May 2027). Notably, I searched the full description and found NO "unrestricted right to work in the U.S." clause on this req - unlike the internship reqs, which all carry it. That is a genuine, if narrow, opening. Relocation to Chicago and a US work visa are still a practical barrier, but the posted qualification bar does not exclude him.

2. Morningstar Development Program - Rotational Track (Campus) | REQ-058222 | Chicago | posted 8 Sep 2026
   https://morningstar.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/morningstar/job/Chicago/Morningstar-Development-Program---Rotational-Track--Campus-_REQ-058222-1
   Verbatim requirements, in full: "A bachelor's degree" / "A resume is required to apply"
   Verbatim: "two-year program... two one-year rotations". Base salary $71,667. No stated graduation year, no stated US work-auth clause, no years-of-experience bar. The loosest posted requirement block of any Morningstar campus req.

3. Morningstar Internship Program - Quantitative Research Intern 2027 (Campus) | REQ-058465 | Chicago | posted 15 Sep 2026
   Verbatim: "Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree in a quantitative or financial discipline (graduating in 2026 or later)." / "Between 0-2 years of professional working experience." / "Familiarity with Python or R for data analysis." / "Basic knowledge of SQL and statistical methods."
   BLOCKER, verbatim: "Must possess unrestricted right to work in the U.S. for this position." $25/hour.
   Content-wise this is the closest match to Omkar's profile in the entire company. The work-auth line kills it.

4. Morningstar Business Summer Internship Program 2027 (Campus) | REQ-058268 | Chicago | posted 8 Sep 2026
   Verbatim: "Currently enrolled in full-time bachelor's degree program, in your third year of study." / "Between 0-2 years of professional work experience."
   BLOCKER, verbatim: "Must possess unrestricted right to work in the U.S. in this position"
   Double blocker: Omkar is in his FINAL (fourth) year, not third. $25/hour. Teams listed: Editorial, Market Intelligence, Product Management, Corporate Design, Manager Research, AI Office.

5. Morningstar Summer Tech Internship Program 2027 (Campus) | REQ-058463 | Chicago | posted 15 Sep 2026
   Verbatim: "The Morningstar Summer Internship Program for Technologists is accepting applicants graduating in 2027." / "Currently enrolled in full-time bachelor's degree program, in their second or third year of study, preferably studying Computer Science." / "Summer interns have the opportunity to apply directly to the Morningstar Development Program after graduation."
   Graduating-2027 line matches him; the "second or third year of study" line does not (he is final-year). Also US-based.

6. Morningstar Internship Program - Sales Intern 2027 (Campus) | REQ-058266 | Chicago - not relevant to his target roles.
7. Morningstar Summer Internship Program - Corporate Finance 2027 (Campus) | REQ-058269 | Chicago - not relevant.
8. Facilities Intern | REQ-058276 | Shenzhen - not relevant.
9. Multilingual Data Analyst Intern | REQ-049644 | Madrid - requires a second European language.

=== B) THE INDIA ENTRY-LEVEL PIPELINE - AND WHY IT IS CLOSED TO HIM ===
"Apprentice" | REQ-057801 | Vashi, Navi Mumbai | posted 23 Sep 2026 (posted YESTERDAY - freshest India req)
https://morningstar.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/morningstar/job/Mumbai/Apprentice_REQ-057801
This is Morningstar India's entry-level factory door, 6-12 month apprenticeship, stipend Rs.22,000/month, and it explicitly teaches "Excel, SQL, and Power BI". It would otherwise be an excellent Jan-2027 bridge. It is HARD-BLOCKED for him by three verbatim lines:
  "Only candidates graduating in 2026 with a Bachelor's degree (preferably in Finance or related non-engineering disciplines) are eligible to apply."
  "Candidates pursuing or holding professional qualifications such as CA, CFA, CMA, CS, ACCA, FRM, or any similar equivalent course are not eligible to apply."
  "BE/B. Tech, Postgraduate, and Master's degree holders are not eligible to apply."
He fails on graduation year (2027, not 2026) AND on degree type (B.Tech is explicitly barred). Do not apply. Do note, however, that this req recurs - a 2027-graduation version may post around mid-2027, but the B.Tech bar would still exclude him.

=== C) WHAT THIS MEANS STRATEGICALLY ===
Morningstar India does NOT run a posted final-semester (Jan-May) internship. Its India entry point is the non-engineering Apprentice track plus "up to 2 years" experienced-hire reqs. For a May-2027 B.Tech grad in Mumbai the realistic paths are:
  (i) Apply now to REQ-058340 (Quantitative Analyst, NPD, "Up to 2 years of experience", Navi Mumbai) and REQ-057918 (Senior Quantitative Analyst, NPD - which states NO years requirement at all). Both are Morningstar Indexes, both Navi Mumbai. Even if the current reqs fill, these two roles have been re-posted repeatedly through 2026 (REQ-057918 since 31 Jul, REQ-056382 since 25 Aug, REQ-058340 since 10 Sep) - Morningstar Indexes Navi Mumbai is clearly hiring continuously at this level. A referral in that team is the highest-leverage single action available.
  (ii) Watch DJSCE campus placements - Morningstar recruits in Mumbai and Navi Mumbai is a 45-minute commute; the India entity hires heavily off local campuses even though the reqs are not tagged "campus" in Workday.
  (iii) Treat REQ-058267 (MDP Equity Research, May-2027 graduation window, no posted US work-auth clause) as a long-shot lottery ticket worth 30 minutes before 5 October 2026.
limitations:
WHAT I GOT, PLAINLY: Full, unrestricted access to Morningstar's live Workday feed. I pulled all 218 global openings, identified all 52 India openings (50 Mumbai, 2 New Delhi), and fetched the complete verbatim job description - including every qualification line - for every India role relevant to this candidate, plus the 2027 campus programmes. Nothing in the roles list is reconstructed or inferred; every qualification block above was copied out of the API's jobDescription field.

WHAT I COULD NOT GET, AND WHY:

1. www.morningstar.com/careers IS BOT-BLOCKED. It returns HTTP 202 with a zero-byte body to curl. I never read the marketing careers site. This matters because if Morningstar runs an India-specific campus or apprenticeship landing page (many GCCs do) outside Workday, I would not have seen it. The Workday feed is authoritative for posted reqs, but a "register your interest for campus hiring 2027" form on the marketing site would be invisible to this method. Worth him checking that page manually in a browser.

2. ONE ROLE'S QUALIFICATIONS ARE INCOMPLETE. REQ-058483 (Sr. Salesforce Administrator, Mumbai, posted 18 Sep 2026) - my extraction captured only the tail of its requirements block, so I do not have its full verbatim qualification text and I have therefore EXCLUDED it from the roles list rather than quote it partially. Based on the fragment I did see it requires Salesforce administration depth he does not have, so the exclusion is unlikely to cost him anything, but I want the gap stated rather than papered over.

3. CHARACTER NORMALISATION. Morningstar's HTML uses typographic characters (curly quotes, en-dashes, the rupee sign). To survive the Windows console encoding I substituted ASCII equivalents: ' for curly apostrophes, " for curly quotes, - for en/em dashes, "Rs." for the rupee glyph. Bullet markers in some reqs were "-", in others "•" - I preserved whichever the source used. NO WORDS, NUMBERS OR REQUIREMENT CLAUSES WERE CHANGED, SHORTENED OR REPHRASED. Where a req had a stray double-bullet ("- - 3-6 years..." in REQ-058334) or a typo ("Ability to remain adapt", "reading XML/Jason", "Customer Succes", "bachelor's degree in engineering" mid-sentence capitalisation), I left it exactly as posted.

4. "POSTED" DATES ARE THE API's startDate FIELD, which is the requisition's posting date. Workday's own displayed label ("Posted 30+ Days Ago") is coarser. I used startDate because it is precise. A "30+ Days Ago" label on a req with a July startDate means it has been open 2-3 months, which usually signals either a hard-to-fill role or a perpetually-open pipeline req - relevant to his odds, so I flagged it in the gists.

5. I DID NOT VERIFY THAT EVERY REQ IS STILL ACCEPTING APPLICATIONS. A req present in the feed is live by definition, but Workday does not expose a "number of applicants" or "about to close" signal. The only explicit closing dates I found anywhere are on the five Chicago 2027 campus reqs, all of which carry the verbatim line "This role will be posted until October 5, 2026."

6. LOCATION GRANULARITY. Workday tags all these roles as "Mumbai". Individual job descriptions repeatedly specify the actual site as "Vashi, Navi Mumbai" (confirmed verbatim in REQ-057801, REQ-058334, REQ-055994, REQ-057577, REQ-058340, REQ-057918, REQ-057834). So the endpoint hint in the task was correct: the India centre is Vashi, Navi Mumbai. I did not find a single Bengaluru or Pune Morningstar opening. The only non-Mumbai India roles are two in New Delhi (REQ-057397 Implementation Consultant, REQ-058293 Infrastructure Engineer).

7. THE AP- VS REQ- PREFIX. India roles appear under two requisition ID series (REQ-0xxxxx and AP-2xxxxxxx). I confirmed these are the same Workday tenant and same company - they are not a separate ATS - but I could not determine what distinguishes them. Notably, REQ-058381 and AP-24869531 are the SAME job (Compliance Analyst, Conflicts of Interest) with word-for-word identical qualifications, posted under two different legal entities (DBRS Ratings GmbH Branch India vs Morningstar India Private Ltd). If he sees apparent duplicates, that is why.

8. NO INDIA INTERNSHIP EXISTS RIGHT NOW - I VERIFIED THIS THREE WAYS. The workerSubType=Intern facet returns exactly 8 jobs globally, zero in India. A free-text search for "intern" returns fuzzy matches only. And the one India entry-level programme (the Apprentice req) explicitly bars B.Tech holders. I want to be unambiguous: I did not fail to find an India internship. There is not one posted. If a Jan-May 2027 final-semester internship at Morningstar India exists, it runs through campus placement or personal referral, not through this portal - which makes the referral channel the decisive one for this candidate at this company.

9. REFERRAL LEVERAGE ASSESSMENT IS MY JUDGEMENT, NOT POSTED FACT. Where I wrote "REFERRAL LEVERAGE: HIGH/VERY HIGH" in the gists, that is inference from req density, team size and how far his years-of-experience sits below the posted bar. Morningstar does not publish referral-pipeline data. Treat those as reasoned opinion, clearly separable from the verbatim qualification text above them.

roles.title: Analyst (Morningstar Credit Analytics - CMBS)
roles.description_gist: A true research-analyst req with a remarkably LOW technical bar: the only tool named is 'Intermediate-level Excel skills'. No SQL, no Python, no BI tool. The work is quantitative and qualitative analysis of loans and properties collateralising CMBS, identifying macro and micro risk factors, and writing monthly research reports and transaction snapshots with commentary and opinion. That last part - written research output - is where his case-competition record does real work (4th of 400+ at IIT Bombay's Ace The Case, Spotify/Datazen winner, IES runner-up all produced written and presented analyses). THE HONEST BLOCKER: '1-3 years relevant experience in the credit research domain, with working knowledge of CMBS transactions.' CMBS is genuinely specialist and cannot be faked. WHAT HE CAN ACTUALLY DO IN 4-6 WEEKS: CMBS fundamentals are well documented and free - read Morningstar DBRS's own published CMBS methodology PDFs at dbrs.morningstar.com, learn DSCR, LTV, debt yield, waterfall/tranching, servicer transfer and special servicing. Combined with his Computational Finance coursework this is a credible story. 'Master's degree, CFA, or FRM preferred' is preferred, not required - do not let it deter the application. REFERRAL LEVERAGE: HIGH - this is a Mumbai offshore-analytics team that hires in volume; a referral moves him past the 'no credit experience' auto-filter.

roles.title: Compliance Analyst, Conflicts of interest, Global Controls
roles.description_gist: THE LOWEST POSTED EXPERIENCE BAR OF ANY ANALYST-TITLED ROLE IN INDIA: 'At least 1 years' experience in operations, roles associated with standardization or experience in an operational business environment.' Note how loose that wording is - 'an operational business environment' is broad enough that his CypherSOL automation-pipeline work and his freelance delivery both count honestly. And then the standout line for him: 'Background or experience in process automation or AI implementation is preferred.' He is unusually strong on exactly that - automation pipelines at CypherSOL, AI+automation for JSW Steel and Abhijeet Plastics at Sereno Volante, automated WhatsApp/SMS re-engagement in his freelance registration platform. Most compliance applicants have zero automation background; he can own that line completely. Gap is domain vocabulary: restricted lists, pre-clearance of employee trades, control room functions, gifts & entertainment monitoring. That is reading, not skill-building - roughly 1-2 weeks with SEBI's and the SEC's public conflict-of-interest guidance plus NISM Series-III A material. Note: '4 days a week in office attendance required.' This req is posted under DBRS Ratings GmbH, Branch India.

roles.title: Specialist, Level II (Data Level II)
roles.description_gist: Morningstar India's core data-operations engine room - collecting operational, document, performance and portfolio data from vendor sources, owning KPIs, resolving client data issues with product and technical teams. Genuinely analytics-adjacent rather than pure entry: it names 'industry/market research, market expansion, process certification, new product development support' as project work, which is squarely his consulting wheelhouse. TWO SPECIFIC UNLOCKS WORTH HIS TIME: (1) 'Good command in MS Office (Excel, PowerPoint etc.); advanced users preferred' - Advanced Excel (Power Query, Power Pivot, pivot models) is ~3 weeks and is the single most repeated requirement across the entire Morningstar India set. (2) 'Continuously improve data collection and quality assurance process using LSS tools' - LSS is Lean Six Sigma. A Six Sigma Yellow Belt or Green Belt primer is a genuine 2-4 week, low-cost certification that directly names a posted requirement, and it transfers to the operations-analyst roles at every other company on his list. That is exactly the kind of small edge-giving credential he asked for. Softer spot: 'Bachelor's degree or above in finance/ business with knowledge in fund investment data' - he is B.Tech CSE, so lead with the Computational Finance coursework and the CypherSOL fintech internship. Requires shift flexibility.

The work is ESG research support for asset owners, asset managers, banks and insurers across APAC/EMEA/Americas - understanding, interpreting and analysing client requests on data or methodology. That is a genuine qualification-crossing exercise, not busywork, and it also upgrades him for half the other roles on this list.

The 'up to 2 years' ceiling means this is deliberately a junior req - they do NOT want someone senior. Python + SQL are 'desirable', not mandatory, and he has both strongly. His Spotify/Datazen EDA win, the IIT Bombay case podium and the Analytrix datathon win all speak directly to 'strong analytical skills + distil complex ideas into simple explanations'. Gaps are domain, not tooling: modern portfolio theory, factor/smart-beta construction, ESG index mechanics. That is 3-5 weeks of self-study (CFA Level I Portfolio Management reading + Morningstar's own public index methodology PDFs at indexes.morningstar.com), not a language he refuses to learn. R and MATLAB are listed as alternatives to Python, so he needs neither. REFERRAL LEVERAGE: VERY HIGH - small specialist team, Navi Mumbai, and the same team has three live reqs at different levels, which means active headcount.

roles.title: Data Scientist (AI & ML, Data Collection - PitchBook)
roles.description_gist: THE STRONGEST TECHNICAL-SKILL OVERLAP OF ANY INDIA REQ. Read this qualification list next to his KOP AI project and the alignment is almost line-for-line: 'transformers, embeddings, RAG, LLMs, prompt engineering, fine-tuning, or agentic workflows' - KOP AI is RAG over PDFs/YouTube with page+timestamp citations, orchestrating 10 stateful LLM agents in parallel. 'Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience using pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn' - he has all five. 'document parsing, preprocessing, chunking, feature engineering, embeddings, RAG, prompt engineering' - LawzyAI is literally LLM query normalisation feeding TF-IDF retrieval. 'precision, recall, F1' - LearnSphere and the ML Quest fake-job-posting classifier. THE BAR IS ONLY '2+ years' and he has ~13 months of internships plus 2 years freelance, which a sympathetic recruiter can read as clearing it. TWO HONEST GAPS: (a) 'PyTorch or TensorFlow' - he has ONNX Runtime and scikit-learn but neither framework named; PyTorch basics are a genuine 3-4 week fix and directly unlock this line. (b) 'Hugging Face, LangChain, or comparable NLP and LLM frameworks' - he uses Groq/ChromaDB/Llama 3.1 directly, so 'comparable' arguably covers him, but a weekend on Hugging Face transformers + a LangChain rebuild of KOP AI's retrieval layer would let him claim it outright. Everything else is already true. REFERRAL LEVERAGE: HIGH - PitchBook Mumbai is a smaller, newer org than core Morningstar.
